title: Building AI Products That Actually Work — Ben Hylak (Raindrop), Sid Bendre (Oleve)
talk_summary: Ben Hylak (Raindrop) argues AI products can't be fully specified up front, so teams need continuous iteration driven by 'signals' (explicit/implicit user-behavior indicators) rather than LM-judge evals, and warns that offline evals and LM-as-judge largely don't predict real-world quality. Sid Bendre (Oleve) presents 'Trellis': discretize the open-ended output space into intents, convert high-value intents into semi-deterministic workflows, and recursively refine within each workflow.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of relying on LLM-as-judge scores or moving offline evals online, they instrument explicit signals (copy, regenerate, thumbs, marked-correct/wrong) and implicit signals (refusals, task failure, user frustration) clustered by intent to find real defects.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the best companies are using highly curated data sets. They're using autogradable evals... they're not really using LM as judges

takeaways.technique: Cluster failures by intent to find unknown defects
takeaways.what_they_do: They group signals into clusters (e.g., all user frustration around one task) and explore by tags/metadata/intent, because the intent changes what the issue actually is.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when you cluster them, it gets very interesting... there's this cluster of user frustration and it's all around people trying to search for tweets

takeaways.technique: Discretize open-ended work into semi-deterministic workflows
takeaways.what_they_do: They classify usage into intents, then convert each high-value intent into a predefined workflow 'broad enough to be useful but narrow enough to be reliable', so each workflow is self-attributable and self-bound.

takeaways.technique: Prioritize by volume × negative sentiment × achievable delta
takeaways.what_they_do: They rank workflows by expected lift: volume times negative sentiment, refined with estimated achievable delta and strategic relevance, instead of volume alone.
takeaways.evidence_quote: negative sentiment times volume times estimated achievable delta times some strategic relevance

takeaways.what_they_do: They favor deterministic pass/fail checks over model judges, and note that eval sets only cover what you already know and saturate quickly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The eval that you collect are only the things you already know of. It's going to be easy to saturate them
